learning_outcomes.text: Development of an adequate expression and technical discussion of own arguments.

Knowledge and understanding of both mathematical principles and the role of mathematical sciences as a tool for the analysis and the problem solving of mechanical engineering problems. Knowledge of the principles of computer science and the algorithmic and numerical approach to problems.

Applying knowledge and understanding related to mathematical methods - with particular reference to differential and integral calculation, geometry, linear algebra, numerical calculation, linear programming and probability and statistical calculation - to model, analyze and solve engineering problems, also with the help of IT tools.

syllabus_topics: First and second order linear Ordinary Differential Equations, with constant or continuous coefficients
Boundary value problems for ODEs, eigenvalues and eigenfunctions
First order quasi-linear and second order linear PDEs with constant coefficients
Boundary value problems for Laplace, heat and wave equations
First order linear equations; the parameter variation method
Second order linear equations with constant or continuous coefficients, homogeneous or not
Methods for obtaining a solution of the non homogeneous equation
Harmonic motion: forced and damped equations
Legendre equation (of order 1) and the d'Alembert method
Boundary value problems for second order equations
The L^2 space: an orthonormal system of periodic functions
Fourier series: pointwise convergence, uniform convergence
Solving PDEs by means of Fourier series: the vibrating string equation and the one dimensional heat equation
Cauchy problem for first order quasi-linear equations
Dirichlet and Neumann problems for the Poisson equation
Cauchy-Dirichlet and Cauchy-Neumann problems for parabolic and hyperbolic equations
Two examples of not well posed problems: the heat equation for t<0 and the Hadamard problem
Radial solutions of the Laplace equation
Solving the wave equation by means of the reflection method
Solving second order non homogeneous linear ordinary differential equations and Dirichlet problems for Laplace and heat equations in a half space, by means of Fourier transforms
The fundamental solution of the heat equation
The Laplace transform: properties and examples
Solving ordinary differential equations and integral-differential equations by means of Laplace transforms
assessment_rules: The student will be assessed through an oral exam. A grade of Fail (Insufficient) indicates serious conceptual errors or a lack of understanding. A grade of 18-22 signifies elementary knowledge with some errors. A grade of 23-25 indicates satisfactory understanding and ability to apply knowledge to familiar contexts. A grade of 26-28 means a solid theoretical understanding and ability to solve problems. A grade of 29-30 and Honors (Lode) indicates complete, in-depth knowledge, critical thinking, originality, and rigor.
